brief: A mustard tile inspired by Mangalagiri cotton: a fine white 8-cell window check with a gold border strip along the bottom edge.

A 64x64 tile inspired by Mangalagiri handloom: 8-cell D4 body check in white on maroon, a 12-cell-tall bottom border of inverted gold checks (period 8) with a single centred dot between every pair of checks, exactly three colours, all marks on a 4x4 cell, border attached to the tile edge.
A white tile crossed by three vertical bands in the order white, red, indigo, with a thin yellow line on each side of the red band.

A black field with a row of four nested diamonds (three concentric levels, alternating red and white) repeating with period 16 along the horizontal axis, bordered top and bottom by a band of alternating red and white triangles whose tips meet to form lozenges, D2-symmetric, four inks.
A white tile with a red border on three sides and a single centred red diamond on an 8 px grid.

A counted-thread panel inspired by the phulam gamosa: red on white, all marks on a 4 px cell grid, a 12-cell-wide motif band at the bottom with a mirror-symmetric row of stepped diamonds and crosses, two plain red stripes 2 cells wide along both long edges.
A black-and-yellow border tile with a double-line outline and a centred diamond filled with evenly spaced diagonal hatching.

A D2-symmetric 64x64 border tile with period 16 along the horizontal axis: a saw-tooth outer edge, a row of double-outlined fish-eye circles, and all enclosed regions filled with parallel hatching at 3 px pitch; four inks (black, turmeric, vermilion, indigo) on a rice-paper ground.
A two-tone wood-ground tile with a single zigzag border band and a centred diamond, mirror-symmetric left-right.

A D2-symmetric 64x64 tile in two inks (wood ground and burnt line) with an outer chevron band of period 8, an inner band of crisscross lines of period 4, and a central lozenge containing a sun disc; line coverage between 20% and 35%.
A red-and-white check tile with 8-cell squares and a thin black border stripe on one edge.

A 64x64 counted-thread tile on an 8x8 cell grid: alternating red and white checks of 2 cells, a 1-cell black pinstripe every 4 cells in the warp direction only, and a 6-cell dobby border band at the bottom whose pattern has translation period 4, all boundaries snapped to the cell grid.
A dark red field with a diamond of 12 small white dots in the centre and one dot in each corner.

A 64x64 counted-grid tile on 4-pixel cells: a 4x4 lattice of stepped diamonds alternating yellow/green on a red ground with a 1-cell black-and-white chequer border, D4 symmetric, no more than 5 colours, every colour boundary on a cell edge.
A rust-red tile with a single large yellow lozenge made of straight stitch runs on a 4-px grid and a white dot at the centre.

A Haryana-bagh-inspired counted-thread tile: a 64x64 grid of 4-px stitch cells fully covered by nested yellow-and-orange lozenges (each large lozenge split into three concentric bands, innermost split into four squares), D4 symmetry on the grid, a zig-zag row of small white lozenges along each border, red ground visible only as 1-cell outlines, maximum five colours.
A brick-red tile with a single stepped white hexagon centred on it and a yellow dot at its core.

A band design inspired by Kullu shawl ends: a symmetric stack of seven horizontal bands on black with widths in ratio 1:2:1:4:1:2:1, palette order yellow-green-white-red-white-green-yellow, each wide band carrying a zigzag with a 16 px period.
A cream-ground tile with six overlapping red circles around a central circle, each circle drawn as a white-red-black triple line.

A C6-rotational Kamalban-inspired field of intersecting circles on a kaolin ground, every circle stroked as three concentric lines in strict white-red-black order, two lattice rings deep, with a row of white dots at fixed 6 px spacing along the bottom dado; four earth colours only.
A black tile inspired by Kasuti: a red stepped-diamond chain in double-running stitch style on a 4-cell grid, mirrored across the centre.

A 64x64 Ilkal-inspired tile: 8-px period indigo pin-stripes on mustard across the body, a 16-px red right-hand border carrying the tope-teni sequence white-red-white-red-white (widths 2-3-6-3-2, mirror-symmetric), and a 2-px peacock-green line separating body and border; five colours max.
A pookalam-inspired disc of four concentric rings (white, orange, yellow, red) with 8-fold rotational symmetry and a green centre.

A 64x64 kasavu-inspired tile: plain cream field, bottom border sequence gold-cream-red-cream-gold with widths 4-2-6-2-4 px (mirror-symmetric), a 1-px green line at the outer edge, three accent colours plus cream, and translation symmetry along x.
An off-white tile with a black checker (choukari) lattice and a small red diamond in every cell.

A 64x64 tile whose top 44 rows are a plain peacock-blue field and whose bottom 20 rows form a reversible border mirrored about row 54: gold 2 px, crimson 3 px, a 4-px band of 2x2 gold-and-blue checks with period 4, crimson 3 px, gold 2 px; at most four colours.
A sparse white-on-ochre tile with a centered square outlined by a dotted line and four small triangles at the corners.

A 64x64 two-colour tile (rice-white on red ochre) with D4 symmetry: a double-ruled central square whose outline is made of dots at period 3, a zigzag frieze of triangles with translation period 8 along all four edges, and total white coverage between 12% and 20%.
A white tile with a single row of black 5-step staircase triangles along the bottom edge.

A cream field with a border strip on both long edges, each carrying a continuous row of 7-step black triangles (base 13 cells, period 13) with the top border inverted so the two rows are mirror images across the horizontal midline; add a thin black line two cells inside each border; two inks.
A black tile with a bottom border strip of four concentric red-and-white diamonds on an 8x8 cell grid.

A dark field with a 16-cell-high bottom border containing a row of nested diamonds (three levels: red, yellow, white) with period 16, a white zig-zag line of period 4 running just above the diamonds, and small white crosses on a 5-cell grid centred between diamond tips; D2 symmetric about the vertical midline, five inks.
A white tile with a central pair of red horizontal bands separated by a thin white line, a green line on each side, and a solid black band across each end.

A field with the mirror-symmetric lengthwise sequence red(9)-green(1)-yellow(1)-blue(1)-red(1)-black(2)-white(7)-black(1)-green(1)-red(1)-white(7) scaled to 64 cells, crossed at right angles by two solid black bands of width 4 at one-third and two-thirds of the height that fully occlude the stripes, with a row of four small yellow triangles centred in each wide white stripe; seven inks.
A red tile with four equal black horizontal bands separated by thin red lines and a single centred row of small white squares.

A black field with a mirror-symmetric band sequence orange-white-black-white-orange (widths 6:1:10:1:6) repeating with period 24 along the vertical axis, a central horizontal row of white 2x2 squares with period 4, and a one-cell white dotted border at each selvedge, four inks, no figurative marks.
A red-and-black chequerboard on an 8-cell grid with a white single-cell rudraksha-dot border on all four sides.

A 64x64 counted grid (cell size 4) in madder red, black and white: a 9x9 saktapar chequerboard centred, framed by a 2-cell border of alternating white dots with translation period 2 cells, D4 symmetry overall, white limited to at most 20% of cells.
A rust-red tile with four yellow lozenges in the corners and a white lozenge in the centre, all on a 4-px stitch grid.

A Bawan-bagh-inspired counted-thread tile: a 64x64 field split into a 4x4 grid of 16-px squares, each square holding a D2-symmetric geometric fill from a set of at least four distinct patterns (nested lozenges, chevrons, zig-zag lines, dots), every mark on a 2-px stitch cell, square borders in yellow, ground visible only as 1-px outlines, maximum five colours including ground.
A cream tile with a black-outlined red four-petal buti in the centre and small indigo dots at the four corners.

A 64x64 tile of 45-degree diagonal bands cycling through exactly five colours in the fixed order yellow, green, magenta, blue, white with widths 6,4,6,4,4 pixels, the pattern repeating with period 24 perpendicular to the bands and tiling seamlessly.
A vertical stripe panel with a repeating group of eight thin stripes in white, red, yellow, green, black, red, white, green.

A stripe design inspired by Lepcha thara: groups of ten vertical stripes with a thick-thin-thin-thick width rhythm, ordered palette white-red-yellow-green-black repeated twice per group, and one band per group carrying a row of sideways chevrons with a 8 px period.
A white single-stroke loop kolam inspired by Tamil sikku kolam on a 3x3 square dot grid, every dot enclosed, D4 symmetric, on a dark ground.

A 64x64 counted-thread panel inspired by Toda embroidery with a 16-cell period along x, three stacked bands (black zigzag, red lozenge chain, black zigzag), D2 symmetry within each period, only red and black on white, no mark off the 4x4 stitch cell, and at least 20% white background.
A red-and-white ikat-inspired tile with a single centred stepped diamond inside a square, D4 symmetric.

A 64x64 tile inspired by Pochampally chowkra: 16-cell period, each cell a stepped diamond-within-square in red and black on white, 4x4 stitch cell, D4 symmetry, exactly three colours, with a 2-cell feathered (stepped) edge on every diamond.
A black tile with vertical stripes in the order red, white, red mirrored about the centre and a thin white line at each edge.

A black field with a vertical stripe sequence white(1)-red(3)-white(1)-black(4) repeating with period 9 and mirrored about the vertical midline, plus a single horizontal row of small white diamonds across the middle on a 3-cell grid, period 9; exactly three inks, black covering at least 50 percent.
A square sandstone jaali panel with a plain 6-pixel frame and a regular grid of 5x5 square holes.

A chikan-jaali-inspired white tile: a bilaterally symmetric paisley outline whose interior is a diagonal (45-degree) net on a 3-px cell grid, every hole on grid, no hole touching the outline, four small corner butis, single ink colour.
A brick-red tile with a white five-pointed star inside a circle and a single white dot at the centre.

A pichhoda-inspired dot field: yellow ground, maroon dots of radius 3 on a staggered lattice with pairwise clearance >= 4 px, C4 symmetry of the dot set about the tile centre, a central dot-free disc of radius 10, and a ring of 12 smaller dots (radius 1) around that disc.
A cream stitch grid with a centred eight-point star and four small corner stars in red, mirror-symmetric on both axes.

A 64x64 counted grid (cell 4) with D4 symmetry: a central 8-point star, four corner kalka-like teardrops pointing inward, a wave border of period 8 cells, and every empty cell row carrying a running-stitch dash of period 2; four thread colours on a cream ground.
A two-tone plaited check on an 8-cell grid, alternating light and dark strips in both directions, mirror-symmetric.

A 64x64 strip grid (cell 4) in two natural tones forming a 2/2 twill diagonal-band repeat with period 4 in both axes, C2 symmetry, a one-cell plain-check border on all sides, and light/dark balance within 45-55%.
A rust-red tile with a centred yellow lozenge and a white dot at each corner, on a 4-px stitch grid.

A phulkari-inspired tile: nested yellow/white/orange lozenges at the centre, four half-lozenges bisected by the tile edges so the pattern tiles seamlessly, D4 symmetry on a 2-px stitch grid, red ground visible only as 1-cell outlines, four colours.
A white-on-brown tile with a centered square drawn in dots and a ring of eight small triangles around it.
state: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu

brief: A 64x64 tile, white on mud-brown with one yellow accent dot at the centre, D4 symmetric: a central square whose sides are dotted at period 2, a surrounding circle of 16 triangles alternating up/down, and all four edges carrying a dash-dot frieze with translation period 6; white coverage 10-18%.
state: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu

brief: A red-sandstone jaali tile with a 6-px solid frame and a 4x4 grid of square holes.

A jaali-inspired screen: hexagonal lattice of hexagonal holes with a six-pointed-star hole at the centre, D2 mirror symmetry, web thickness >= 3 px everywhere, one connected solid attached to a 4-px frame, 40-50% open area, two colours (sandstone and void).
A light-wood panel with a grid of eight-pointed star cut-outs separated by a dark connected web.

A lattice inspired by Khatamband: a 64x64 panel of eight-pointed stars and interstitial squares with D4 symmetry, a single connected web at least 3 px wide everywhere, attached to a 4 px frame, repeating every 32 px in both axes.
A maroon field with a 4x4 lattice of small white rings, each with a maroon centre dot.

A dot field inspired by Ladakhi thigma: 24 white rings on maroon arranged in two offset rows along a horizontal strip, centres at least 10 px apart, alternating every third ring with a small cross, mirror symmetric about the strip's vertical centre line.
A coir-brown tile with a simple 8 px check of cream squares.

A counted-grid mat tile inspired by Lakshadweep coir weaves: a 4 px cell grid, a two-axis check in coir brown and cream with every fourth row replaced by a red-green stripe pair, a centred twill diamond with D2 symmetry, four colours maximum.
A white sikku-style loop inspired by Puducherry threshold kolam on a 2x2 dot grid, one closed stroke, D4 symmetric.

A kolam-inspired figure on a 5x5 square dot grid drawn as exactly two closed strokes that together enclose all 25 dots, with D4 symmetry, isolated crossings only, white on dark ground, and a wave-like outer ring of 8 equal lobes.
